name: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
lead: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH, corticotropin) is a 39-amino-acid hormone released by the anterior pituitary gland. It tells the adrenal glands to make cortisol and other steroid hormones, and it sits at the centre of the body's stress-response (HPA) axis [12]. In looksmaxxing and recovery circles it comes up because the same precursor molecule, POMC, also yields alpha-MSH, the signal that drives skin pigmentation, and because cortisol levels influence skin, fat distribution, sleep and muscle.

ACTH acts through the melanocortin 2 receptor (MC2R), the only receptor for which it is the natural agonist, and the receptor needs a helper protein (MRAP) to reach the cell surface [1]. Related melanocortin receptors respond to ACTH fragments and to alpha-MSH, which is why very high ACTH in Addison's disease is accompanied by darker skin [12][2].

Pharmaceutical corticotropin (sold as Acthar Gel and in synthetic forms such as cosyntropin/tetracosactide) is a prescription injectable used by physicians, for example for infantile spasms and as a diagnostic test of adrenal function [12]. Registered clinical trials have studied it in nephrotic syndrome, multiple sclerosis, uveitis and rheumatoid arthritis [3][4][5][6]. Its use as a self-directed appearance aid is not described in the published literature; discussion centres on stress, cortisol and tanning-related biology.

chain: ACTH signals the adrenals to make cortisol
Cortisol balance shapes sleep, recovery, skin and fat distribution
angle.text: People interested in recovery and skin look at ACTH because it sets the cortisol rhythm that affects sleep, training recovery and facial puffiness, and because it belongs to the same family as the melanocortins that darken skin. In practice it is a prescription hormone given by clinicians rather than a product used for aesthetics.

paras: ACTH is cut from a larger precursor, proopiomelanocortin (POMC), which also produces alpha-MSH, beta-endorphin and CLIP [12]. The hypothalamus releases corticotropin-releasing hormone, which prompts pituitary ACTH release; cortisol then feeds back to dampen both signals [12].

In the adrenal cortex, MC2R activation raises cAMP and switches on steroid-making enzymes, producing cortisol and, from the zona reticularis, androgens [12][1]. Cloning of the melanocortin receptor family in 1992 clarified how ACTH and the MSH peptides act on different tissues [7].

Alpha-MSH, which shares its amino-terminal sequence with ACTH, stimulates melanin production in skin [12]. A major review describes the hormonal regulation of mammalian skin pigmentation, including the role of POMC products [8]. In Addison's disease, low cortisol leaves ACTH chronically high, and hyperpigmentation is a recognised sign [12].

Corticotropin preparations are prescribed for infantile spasms and have been trialled in several immune and kidney conditions [12][3][4][5][6]. Synthetic ACTH fragments are used to test adrenal reserve [12].

Clinical work on the ACTH axis also includes diagnosing Cushing's syndrome, where tumours or other causes drive excess cortisol, and the development of ACTH receptor antagonists as investigational tools [9][1].

Registered trials include ACTH for relapsing nephrotic syndrome (n=31, phase 3) [3], diabetic nephropathy proteinuria [10], multiple sclerosis myelination and fatigue [4][11], uveitis [5] and rheumatoid arthritis with methotrexate [6]. No published trials have tested ACTH for cosmetic or physique goals.

Because ACTH raises cortisol, prolonged exposure can produce features seen in Cushing's syndrome, including weight gain, skin thinning and mood changes [9]. Medicinal corticotropin is dispensed under medical supervision.

timeline.event: Collip, Anderson and Thomson describe the adrenotropic hormone in The Lancet [12].
Klaus Hofmann's active synthetic fragment of ACTH (first 23 amino acids) is reported in the press [12].
The melanocortin receptor family, including the ACTH receptor, is cloned [7].

card.summary: The pituitary hormone that sets cortisol output and sits in the same family as the skin-darkening melanocortins; given by prescription as corticotropin.

quick.overview:
ACTH is the pituitary signal that tells your adrenal glands to make cortisol. Cortisol rhythm affects sleep, recovery, skin and where the body stores fat, which is why the topic appears in recovery and appearance discussions.

It comes from the same precursor as alpha-MSH, the peptide behind skin pigmentation. Medicinal versions such as Acthar Gel and cosyntropin are used by doctors for conditions like infantile spasms and adrenal testing.
quick.mechanism: ACTH binds the MC2R receptor on adrenal cells, raising cAMP and driving cortisol and androgen production. Cortisol feeds back to the brain to lower further ACTH release.
quick.risks: Raising ACTH raises cortisol; extended exposure is associated with Cushing-type features such as weight gain, skin thinning and mood effects. It is a prescription-only product.
